description: Registered cancellation suppresses ungranted wrong-path lower reads. Timing-accepted, physically tested 62.5 MHz profile with complete CoreMark, Linux application, mesh, software-audit and bounded cache-experiment evidence.

root_cause.observation: The registered cancellation previously permitted an old PTE_REQ/ACCESS_REQ to request/grant DDR on the cancellation edge, forcing the redirect to drain unnecessary traffic.
root_cause.change: When PIPE_FETCH and RESTART_ON_CANCEL are enabled, a registered fetch_cancel suppresses the ungranted lower request before arbitration.
preserved_contracts: RESTART_ON_CANCEL=0 retains the legacy live-EX cancellation behavior.
Already granted reads are in WAIT and retain ownership until their response drains without a stale token/fill/fault.
The cancellation gate consumes a registered frontend signal; it does not restore a combinational EX-to-lower-arbitration path.

+++ cpu62/etc/workloads-sqlite-PUBLIC-DOMAIN.txt
@@ -1,24 +1,32 @@
-/******************************************************************************
-** This file is an amalgamation of many separate C source files from SQLite
-** version 3.54.1.  By combining all the individual C code files into this
-** single large file, the entire code can be compiled as a single translation
-** unit.  This allows many compilers to do optimizations that would not be
-** possible if the files were compiled separately.  Performance improvements
-** of 5% or more are commonly seen when SQLite is compiled as a single
-** translation unit.
+/*
+** 2001-09-15
 **
-** This file is all you need to compile SQLite.  To use SQLite in other
-** programs, you need this file and the "sqlite3.h" header file that defines
-** the programming interface to the SQLite library.  (If you do not have
-** the "sqlite3.h" header file at hand, you will find a copy embedded within
-** the text of this file.  Search for "Begin file sqlite3.h" to find the start
-** of the embedded sqlite3.h header file.) Additional code files may be needed
-** if you want a wrapper to interface SQLite with your choice of programming
-** language. The code for the "sqlite3" command-line shell is also in a
-** separate file. This file contains only code for the core SQLite library.
+** The author disclaims copyright to this source code.  In place of
+** a legal notice, here is a blessing:
 **
-** The content in this amalgamation comes from Fossil check-in

+**    May you do good and not evil.
+**    May you find forgiveness for yourself and forgive others.
+**    May you share freely, never taking more than you give.
 **
-**    
+*************************************************************************
+** This header file defines the interface that the SQLite library
+** presents to client programs.  If a C-function, structure, datatype,
+** or constant definition does not appear in this file, then it is
+** not a published API of SQLite, is subject to change without
+** notice, and should not be referenced by programs that use SQLite.
+**
+** Some of the definitions that are in this file are marked as
+** "experimental".  Experimental interfaces are normally new
+** features recently added to SQLite.  We do not anticipate changes
+** to experimental interfaces but reserve the right to make minor changes
+** if experience from use "in the wild" suggest such changes are prudent.
+**
+** The official C-language API documentation for SQLite is derived
+** from comments in this file.  This file is the authoritative source

+**
+** The name of this file under configuration management is "sqlite.h.in".
+** The makefile makes some minor changes to this file (such as inserting
+** the version number) and changes its name to "sqlite3.h" as
+** part of the build process.
 */

interpretation: Only the initramfs pathname differs in the kernel config; all configuration selections match.
Both archives contain the same 37 paths in the same order. The only changed content is a corrected SQLite copyright-disclaimer text; all 36 other entry contents match.
Metadata-only differences affect 25 directory/symlink/device entries through mtime; the license entry also changes mtime and filesize.
Kernel Image bytes differ. This audit establishes config and initramfs content differences, not byte identity of executable kernel sections.
The later b207eb2 versus 099154d correction uses exactly the same CPU62 Linux payload, isolating that hardware change in its model/board comparison.

comparisons_to_previous_store_profile.scope: Complete physical profiles at different clocks; not an isolated IPC or OS-overhead experiment.

notes: The preceding b207eb2 evidence remains immutable; this candidate has a distinct physical build tag.
Three bare-metal and three Linux performance samples plus one validation-seed sample in each environment pass CRC and duration checks. Pilot samples are not accepted scores.

Bare-metal throughput improves 5.24 percent over the previous 58.823529 MHz profile; Linux CoreMark decreases 0.46 percent. Application gains are 2.06 to 2.79 percent at a 6.25 percent higher CPU clock, not per-MHz gains.

Linux images have identical application binaries; exact kernel-config and initramfs differences are recorded in the software audit. The direct b207eb2-to-099154d comparison uses the same CPU clock and exact Linux image.

Lower-bus read reduction and the fail-before/pass-after regression establish the eliminated traffic mechanism. Counter events overlap and are not an additive CPI breakdown. Linux profiler counters include the whole CPU during each command.
The frozen UART stops at the final benchmark mesh completion. The separately retained live reader and 64-point demo continue after that immutable evidence boundary.
